proved_step: REPAIRED LEMMA (window + Sperner atom bound, exact scope). Setting: integer weights w_1..w_n, threshold t, restriction R in which each variable is independently free (prob 1/3), fixed to 0 (1/3) or fixed to 1 (1/3). Let F = free set, G = fixed set, Y = sum of w_j over fixed-1 j, b_j in {0,1} the fixed values, s = #{j in G: w_j != 0}, W_F = sum_{j in F} (max(0,w_j) - min(0,w_j)), mn_F = sum_{j in F} min(0,w_j), mx_F = sum_{j in F} max(0,w_j). Claim: P(gate nonconstant | F) <= min(1, W_F * C(s, floor(s/2)) / 2^s) <= min(1, W_F / sqrt(s)) for s >= 1. Proof. (1) Gate g = [sum_F x_j w_j + Y >= t] over free x. Its value set over free x is {0,1} iff mn_F + Y < t <= mx_F + Y, i.e. Y in (t - mx_F, t - mn_F - 1]... precisely iff t - Y in (mn_F, mx_F]. This interval contains exactly W_F integers, so P(nonconst | F) = P(Y in a set of W_F integers). (2) Erdos (1945) / Sperner: for nonzero integers |w_j| >= 1, j in G, each value y is attained by at most C(s, floor(s/2)) subsets of G; hence P(Y = y) <= C(s,floor(s/2))/2^s for every y. (3) Union bound over the W_F integers gives the first inequality; min with 1 is trivial. (4) C(s,floor(s/2))/2^s <= 1/sqrt(s) for s >= 1 (standard central-binomial bound). Scope: exact for every integer weight vector and threshold; the 1/3-model enters only through the law of F. Consequence (decay regime): if W_F = o(sqrt(s)) then P(nonconst | F) -> 0. For unit weights this is f = o(sqrt(n)) free variables. At constant free fraction it gives NO decay (E[W_F] ~ n/3 >> sqrt n), consistent with cm-64653810efde4130.
